title: Training Note: The Answer Share in Employer Benefit Charging Protests
content:
This training note covers the answer share that applies when an employer protests in writing the Employer Benefit Charging charges on a statement, disputing its base-period wages or its base-period status. The answer share reflects how the employer answered the notice of claim on that position.

**Rule.** The answer share is four fifths (0.80) when no separation response to the notice of claim is on record for the position, nine tenths (0.90) when the separation response on record was received after the response due date without good cause, and the whole (1.00) otherwise.

**Q. What does "on record" mean here?**
A. The employer's submissions on the position: a separation response is on record when a separation-response submission appears among them. When none appears, the answer share is 0.80, whatever the position's status.

**Q. How is "after the response due date" judged?**
A. By comparing the response date recorded on the position with the response due date recorded on the position. A response date later than the due date is after it; a response received on the due date is not.

**Q. What if the response was late but the employer showed good cause?**
A. A response recorded as late with good cause shown is not "without good cause", so the answer share is the whole, 1.00.

**Q. Which cases fall to the whole?**
A. A response on record received on or before the due date, and a late response with good cause shown. Both give 1.00.

**Summary card (hypothetical positions)**

| Separation response on record | Received | Good cause shown | Answer share |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | — | — | 0.80 |
| Yes | Two days after the due date | No | 0.90 |
| Yes | Two days after the due date | Yes | 1.00 |
| Yes | On the due date | — | 1.00 |
